text.title: langchain-observability Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules for instrumenting LangChain chains with LangSmith, structured callbacks, redaction, sampling, and streaming.

rule.statement: Enable LangSmith tracing from day one of production. Retrofitting tracing after an incident captures none of the data needed to debug it.
rule.rationale: Intermediate steps, token usage, and tool calls are only captured during the live run. Without tracing the only debug surface is application logs, which miss the LLM step entirely.

rule.statement: Assert LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=true at app boot in production; refuse to start the service if missing.
rule.rationale: A silent off-switch on tracing has historically led to long outages where 'we have no idea what happened'. Treat it as required infrastructure.

rule.statement: When pii_posture is internal or no-export, attach a redaction callback BEFORE the LangSmith handler.
rule.rationale: Trust no upstream sanitization; the call site is the only place you can guarantee redaction. SSNs and email addresses must never reach the trace UI.

rule.statement: Override on_chain_error in any custom CallbackHandler with raise_error=True or a dead-letter push. Default behavior swallows exceptions.
rule.rationale: BaseCallbackHandler swallows callback exceptions by design to protect chains; this hides bugs in observability code itself.

rule.statement: For production sampling, either trace at 1.0 for the first 30 days, or use tail-based sampling that keeps every run with status=error.
rule.rationale: Uniform low-rate sampling misses the rare failures you most need to see. Either trace everything early, or sample by outcome.

rule.statement: Enable streaming when latency_target_ms ≤ 500. The UX cliff falls fast below 500ms perceived latency.
rule.rationale: Streaming first-token latency dominates user perception; below 500ms users perceive instant response.

rule.statement: Set LANGCHAIN_PROJECT per deployment environment (dev/staging/prod); never share a single project across envs.
rule.rationale: Shared projects mix noisy dev traffic with prod, hiding real incidents.

rule.statement: For pii_posture=no-export, fall back to opentelemetry to a local collector; never use the hosted LangSmith endpoint.
rule.rationale: Regulated workloads cannot leak payloads to a third-party SaaS, even for debugging.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, pii_posture is public or internal, latency_target_ms is above 500 and cost_cap_per_turn_usd is 0.01 or less, the decision-record MUST set tracing_backend=langsmith and sample_rate=0.1 (LANGCHAIN_TRACING_SAMPLE_RATE=0.1) AND keep every run with status=error in full. Because the env sample rate decides at run start and cannot see the outcome, the error keep is implemented in the custom CallbackHandler's on_chain_error path (or an equivalent run-level tracing toggle), and audit.rule_refs cites r5. Streaming is not forced on this branch.

rationale.source: LangSmith documentation (LANGCHAIN_TRACING_SAMPLE_RATE); tail-based sampling practice as described in the OpenTelemetry Collector docs

rule.rationale: At a one-cent turn cap the trace of every turn costs a visible share of the turn, so uniform sampling is the honest default, but uniform sampling at 10% sees one error in ten. LangSmith's sample-rate variable is head-based by design; the tail-based keep is what turns a cheap sample into a debuggable one, and r5 exists for exactly this trade.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, pii_posture is public or internal, latency_target_ms is above 500 and cost_cap_per_turn_usd is above 0.01, the decision-record MUST set tracing_backend=langsmith and sample_rate=1.0 (LANGCHAIN_TRACING_SAMPLE_RATE=1.0), and MUST leave streaming at the profile's own value rather than forcing it. The env block carries LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=true and a per-environment LANGCHAIN_PROJECT; redact_payloads=true whenever pii_posture is internal. Lowering the rate later is a new decision-record after the 30-day window in r5, not an env edit.

rationale.source: LangSmith documentation (tracing configuration); this methodology's 04-procedure step 3

rule.rationale: With budget for the trace and no latency cliff there is no reason to drop a run: full tracing is the cheapest possible incident insurance, and the intermittent failures in this methodology's Applies-If are by definition the ones a sample misses. Forcing streaming here would change the chain's output shape for a UX benefit the profile did not ask for.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid and pii_posture is no-export, the decision-record MUST set tracing_backend=opentelemetry (or none), redact_payloads=true, and an OTLP endpoint (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT) that resolves inside the deployment's own network boundary. The env block MUST NOT contain LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=true or a LANGCHAIN_ENDPOINT pointing at api.smith.langchain.com, and the RedactingHandler stays attached ahead of the OTel exporter so the local collector also never stores raw SSNs or emails.

rationale.source: OpenTelemetry documentation (OTLP exporter configuration); LangSmith documentation (data retention)

rule.rationale: LangSmith's hosted endpoint stores full inputs and outputs of every traced run; for a workload that may not export payloads the only compliant trace sink is one the team operates. OpenTelemetry's OTLP exporter is configured by endpoint env var, so the boundary is checkable from the env block alone, and the local collector is still a datastore, which is why redaction stays on.

rule.statement: When the profile is valid, pii_posture is public or internal, and latency_target_ms is 500 or below, the decision-record MUST set tracing_backend=langsmith, streaming=true and sample_rate=1.0 (LANGCHAIN_TRACING_SAMPLE_RATE=1.0), with trace upload running off the request path (LANGCHAIN_CALLBACKS_BACKGROUND=true; check the current default for your LangChain version) so first-token latency is not paid for by the tracer. The cost cap does not reduce the sample rate on this branch; redact_payloads=true whenever pii_posture is internal.

rationale.source: LangSmith documentation (tracing sampling and background callbacks); this methodology's 04-procedure step 3

rule.rationale: A sub-500 ms target is a streaming target, and streaming failures (a stall after the first token, a tool call that never returns) are the ones application logs cannot reconstruct, so head sampling below 1.0 throws away the runs that matter most. LangChain's documentation makes callbacks blocking or background by an env switch, and a synchronous trace upload of a few hundred milliseconds eats the whole latency budget.
